fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the main residence without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway edges so emergency vehicles can pass without being slowed or blocked by overhanging branches.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Remove or thin dense vegetation growth close to the walls of both structures so responders can work around the exterior of each building.
• Mark any gate or pathway at the rear of the property with a visible sign or reflective marker so responders can locate it quickly under low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep any rear gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock to allow responder access without delay.
• Identify and mark a staging area in the open lawn area where emergency vehicles can park, turn around, or position equipment without blocking the single driveway access point.
• Thin dense vegetation at the street frontage so the driveway entrance and address marker are visible to approaching responders from the roadway.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure walls.
• Separate the scattered trees from nearby vegetation by removing the grass, shrubs, or brush growing beneath and between them.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees surrounding the structure so fire cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Trim back vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles at all times.
• Remove overhanging branches above the driveway that could fall and block access.
• Thin shrubs and plants around the perimeter of the structure so open ground is visible between plantings.
• Cut back any plants or branches that make direct contact with the roof, walls, or windows of the structure.
• Mow or cut down tall grass and low vegetation in the open terrain areas immediately surrounding the structure.
• Remove dead branches, leaves, and dry plant material from beneath trees near the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath tree clusters clear of accumulated dead leaves, pine needles, and dry debris.
